subject: geography
title: Globalisation
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Globalisation.

concepts.def: KOF measures economic, social, political dimensions; UK ranks highly; globalisation accelerated after 1980s neoliberalism.
Standardised shipping containers from 1956 (Malcolm McLean); cut transport costs 90%, enabled global supply chains.
Operate across borders: Apple (US designed, Chinese assembled, global retail); 500 largest TNCs control 70% of world trade.
TNCs locate HQ in HICs, manufacturing in NEEs/LICs to cut costs; e.g. Foxconn factories in Shenzhen.
1944 founded IMF, World Bank, GATT (now WTO); promote free trade, criticised for SAPs imposing austerity on LICs.
TNCs adapting global products to local markets; McDonald's McSpicy Paneer (India), Maharaja Mac, Italian salads.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Globalisation — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Globalisation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Globalisation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the KOF Index measure?

numericals.q: Top 500 TNCs control roughly what percentage of trade?

free_texts.q: Name the adaptation of global brands to local markets.
